idiom_name: Foundation XMLDocument/XMLNode tree (with XSLT) / string interpolation
implementation_notes: On Apple platforms Foundation provides the XML tree API: XMLDocument(xmlString:options:) parses, XMLElement/XMLNode with addChild builds markup programmatically, xmlData serializes, and object(byApplyingXSLTString:arguments:) applies a stylesheet for the declarative route. Elsewhere, and for HTML, the idiomatic form is string interpolation into a String with an explicit escape helper. The classic transformer type remains justified when the same data must feed several formats through a shared protocol.
pitfalls: XMLDocument is a reference type with strict parent/child ownership: adding a node that already has a parent raises an exception, so create fresh nodes per document.
An XMLDocument instance is thread-safe only when confined to one thread; do not share one document across concurrent requests.

The XMLDocument tree and XSLT APIs are part of Apple's Foundation (macOS/macCatalyst per Apple's documentation), so cross-platform server code must treat them as platform-specific and fall back to interpolation or a third-party XML library.

variants.name: Interpolation into a String
variants.implementation_notes: The portable idiom: a function that maps the domain to a String with interpolation and one escape helper, streamed into the response; it works identically on Apple platforms and Linux and needs no XML dependency. Choose it when the output is HTML or text rather than XML and the markup is assembled conditionally.
pitfalls: String interpolation does not escape: every interpolated value must go through esc(_:) or user data injects markup.
Large responses built by repeated string concatenation allocate heavily; write into a single result buffer or stream instead.
